Arcanis' Legacy: The Rise of Guar
Synopsis:
In the steampunk, medieval, magical world of
Arcanis
, the malevolent entity Guar, a sentient plague, moves from world to world, spreading chaos and turning inhabitants into demons who do his bidding. Thousands of years ago, five great wizards wielded powerful artifacts embedded with magical crystals that granted them the strength to stand against Guar. As they neared the end of their lives, they hid the crystals in five sacred temples and cast a powerful protection spell over their world. Unable to manifest in his true form due to this spell, Guar strikes a sinister deal with the malevolent king, Nork, promising immense power in exchange for the crystals. Driven by ambition and greed, Nork plunges the world into darkness, sending out spies to locate the artifacts.
You, Kai, a young warrior whose hometown was decimated for resisting Nork's rule, joins a resistance movement to thwart Nork and his master, Guar. Alongside your best friend Kross, the perpetually positive warrior Natalie, and the powerful young mage Lucidius, you embark on a perilous journey to retrieve the hidden crystals before Nork can harness their power.
Experience the rpg of a lifetime based on Dragon Quest and Final Fantasy!

@Trihan

Click to expand...
First of all, the synopsis sounds interesting. I would definitely give a game with that premise a try. And what is here definitely has promise that with some polish could be really good. However:
1. I get that you're enthusiastic, but your marketing speak is bordering on the delusionally confident. Is it really the RPG of a lifetime? That's usually something for the player to decide, not the developer.
2. Similarly, calling your own story "wonderful" is an orange flag to me. If the story is truly wonderful, it should stand on its own and that shouldn't have to be explicitly said. I get that you're trying to develop a commercial product here, and that will involve a degree of self-aggrandising, but when you don't have anything behind that backing you up, it comes across as a lack of confidence in the ability of your work to be good on its own merits. It's kind of a "telling rather than showing" situation, I feel.
3. I know you've said that everything is subject to change, and that's fine, but the maps you're currently showing have a number of issues. You've clearly got a feel for mapping out areas, but you have what I used to refer to as Huge Map Syndrome (and I used to do this exact same thing myself back in 2001 when I started); every space is several times larger than it actually needs to be. You've got what looks like a dungeon that's based in a natural cavern but is somehow symmetrical despite nature not being. If it's been carved out of a cavern, have some natural variance in it. By a similar token, the spike traps in the second screenshot seem to be pretty haphazardly placed and don't make sense: who put them there? What is their purpose? They're too far apart and easily avoided to really work as a deterrent to trespassers. I do like that you've done some varied elevation, though.
4. As it stands currently, even at the price point you've stated, I'm not sure I'd be interested enough to buy it for that. I'd have to see what it turns into, or at least have the option of a demo.
I do look forward to seeing how it develops, though!

This is where ludonarrative dissonance comes into play, somewhat.
Yes, it makes sense for them to be there in the context of it being a running course where you have to get to the end before the timer runs out. That handily takes care of the game part of it.
But in the narrative of the game, the character is currently actually in this physical location that someone built. From that perspective, why are they there? Did someone intentionally create a running course for someone to get to the end of?
That's one part that new developers sometimes forget to incorporate: the idea that these areas are not just set pieces in your game that only exist to provide a gameplay mechanic. They're supposed to be modelling actual places your characters are present in, and it pays dividends to approach your map design as if you're creating real locations and thinking about how someone would actually have built it.

It's caught my eye, from what I've seen via the pictures. Agree with most everything Trihan said (especially this ludonarrative dissonance!!).
One thing I want to touch on is the 'Huge Map Syndrome' because it's something I struggled with a lot and ended up having to redo most of my maps (even now they're probably too big). It really just comes down to negative space. Using your most recent picture of the inside of a building: there are a ton of empty, blue carpet tiles.
That

Looking forward to seeing some combat! Keep up the great work!

posts.body:
My quick thoughts on the battle demo video:
There's a lot of telling. "this system is very strategy focused! this system is very balanced!" stuff like that. You shouldn't have to tell me that, the battle system should speak for itself. Obviously it's still early and things will change, but from the snippet we saw it seems (and I don't mean this negatively) basic. There doesn't appear to be anything special or unique; it is characters using standard attacks and stantard magic spells.
Now all I know about this system is what you said and the brief video, so maybe there is more to come and I'm sure you know a lot more about how it plays than we do, I'm just giving my thoughts on what I saw.
The rolling HP mechanic reminds me of Earthbound. In that game, if you were quick enough you could save someone before they died due to HP slowly scrolling down. I don't know if that is the case here but it also seems like it would take too long, so I'm not sure what the point is. It does look cool though I'll say that! I like the dynamic camera in battle! I can see some people not liking it due to the movement, but I think it is neat. Maybe if it was an option for people? But that is purely your decision on the matter, as it's a style choice.
Overall: it's fine. There's nothing inherently bad about what you showed, it just is lacking that spark that makes it click. And I am certain there is more to come and I am looking forward to see what else you're cooking up! This is a question more for yourself to think about, but: At its core, what is your battle system
about?
Octopath Traveler's system is about
breaking the enemy with weaknesses.
FF7 Remake is about
pressuring and staggering the enemy
.
You're doing great work, games are not easy at all to make and balanced, fun, and engaging battle systems are even harder. But I can tell you've got the ambition and you've got more behind the scenes. I can't wait to see more! Keep it up!

posts.author: TotalyNate

Thanks you for the feedback
@Meowsticks
I'm really trying to keep the battle system simple, thus the simple spells and stuff, in terms of spells,I'm trying to just keep it basic ff style, different elements, and casting effects... maybe it's TOO simple... I'm not sure yet...
This battle system is really all about knowing who your fighting, each enemy has its own "strategy" as it were, and you must figure out this strategy to be able to successfully beat the enemy on a consistent basis.  For example, those gnomes like to use healing spells when they are weak, some enemies love to cast weakening spells THEN attack... and so on... a boss may seem unbeatable until you find a certain skill or spell that levels the playing field, things like that.
Your definitely right about some things not being quite finished, but I'm glad you are happy with the progress so far.

posts.body:
UPDATE!
Hello! Sry for not posting an update in a while! In case you didn't know, I got in an atv accident that made me unable to develop for a couple of weeks. Now I'm back and ready to continue making Arcanis' Legacy: Rise of Guar!
This update is ABSOLUTELY MASSIVE, (as you may also of heard me say), so I won't be showing screenshots of every map I made.
To run it down, here are the things I changed.
New Tilesets:
I have had access to some dlc tilesets for a long time now, I just didn't implement them... well... because I'm lazy. I finally worked up the motivation to do so, and now all the maps, (in my opinion), look MUCH better, the tilesets keep the look of the rtp fresh by redoing most of the tiles.
I also re-mapped the "tower of doom" map since I did not like the purple color I had chosen. I have made several new-maps and a crap-ton of enemies, but I find it unnecessary to show everything, although if you want to see more, please ask!!!
In addition, I also imported music from the same dlc, I still use a couple rtp tracks, but it's mostly all new!
(I've been playing around with different fonts and menu layouts, if you prefer any of my previous choices, let me know.)
Class redo:
After much consideration, I decided to COMPLETELY redo the class system, and while now the damage of spells is reduced, you can now...
Cast debuffs and buffs.
Apply states.
Use dual-cast/tri-cast (in development) to increase damage.
Have all sorts of "non-magic" skills to use, like protecting, counter-attacks, martial-arts based attacks, and so much more!
Enchant weapons with magic to create a "spell-blade" sort of effect!
So basically, the combat now has much more strategy to it, instead of just basic spells and stuff, you can apply all sorts of different combat techniques! Also, I finally finished tweaking the stat-distribution plugin, so everything there is up and running.
CONCLUSSION:
Arcanis' Legacy is coming together very well, it's going from an rpg-maker project, to an actual rpg!!! I would say I'm about 60%-70% done with the game. I have done multiple small fixes like, reducing difficulty, reducing difficulty again, (maybe one more time), spelling errors have been corrected, as well as grammar errors. I am open to feedback AS WELL as releasing a video detailing more of the changes I have made if yall want me to!!!
(For those people out there who love a challenge, DON'T worry, even though the base game is much easier, there are 2 different difficulty modes ABOVE normal, Combat mode and Hell mode, so if it's too easy you can change the difficulty at ANY TIME during the game)
